source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet - oracle-label result
finding: Prior gains from self-correction on reasoning used the ground-truth label to decide when to stop. With that oracle, accuracy rises a lot.
numbers: GPT-3.5: GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3, CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 89.7, HotpotQA 26.0 to 29.0. GPT-4: GSM8K 95.5 to 97.5, CommonSenseQA 82.0 to 85.5, HotpotQA 49.0 to 59.0. One oracle self-correction run.
quote: these results can only be regarded as indicative of an oracle's performance
limits: Oracle labels are not available in real use; the paper says these numbers show only what an oracle can do. Table text was garbled in extraction; pairing read from row order.
agent_relevance: Any gain seen only when code knows the right answer is not self-correction. Supports G2: the signal must come from real output or a check.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet - intrinsic self-correction drops
finding: Without oracle labels, asking the model to review and revise its own answer lowers accuracy on all three reasoning sets and both main models.
numbers: GPT-3.5: CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 (round 1, 3 calls) to 41.8 (round 2, 5 calls); GSM8K 75.9 to 75.1 to 74.7; HotpotQA 26.0 to 25.0 to 25.0. GPT-4: GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0; CSQA 82.0 to 79.5 to 80.0; HotpotQA 49.0 to 49.0 to 43.0.
limits: Test sets are subsets; one main prompt family in this table.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for G1/G2: a blind second look costs accuracy and 2 to 4 extra calls.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet - GPT-4-Turbo and Llama-2
finding: Same drop for other models. The weaker open model falls the most.
numbers: GPT-4-Turbo GSM8K 91.5 to 88.0 (round 1) to 90.0 (round 2); CSQA 84.0 to 81.5 to 83.0. Llama-2 GSM8K 62.0 to 43.5 to 36.5; CSQA 64.0 to 37.5 to 36.5.
limits: Llama-2 size not re-checked in the text read.
agent_relevance: Weaker models are the most harmed by a self-review step; do not use it by default.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet - prompt sensitivity
finding: Three other feedback prompts were tried on GPT-4-Turbo and Llama-2. None beat the plain answer.
limits: Only three prompts. Does not rule out a better prompt.
agent_relevance: Prompt wording changes the size of the loss, not its sign.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet - why: answer flipping
finding: The model keeps its first answer most of the time. When it changes, correct-to-wrong flips outnumber wrong-to-correct. The authors say the model cannot judge its own reasoning.
numbers: GPT-3.5 on GSM8K keeps the initial answer 74.7% of the time over two rounds. CSQA flips far more because wrong options look relevant.
quote: Introducing feedback can be viewed as adding an additional prompt, potentially skewing the model
limits: Flip counts are in a figure; only the 74.7% was read as text.
agent_relevance: Track flips by type in our own tests: net gain is fixes minus breaks.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet - debate vs self-consistency
finding: Multi-agent debate does no better than self-consistency at the same number of responses.
numbers: GSM8K (GPT-3.5): single answer 76.7; self-consistency with 9 responses reaches 88.2 against debate near 83 at 9 responses.
limits: Table 7 columns were misaligned in extraction; only the summary claim and the 76.7 and 88.2 figures are trusted, others omitted.
agent_relevance: Matches G9 (no debate). Voting is the stronger baseline.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
finding: One model writes, critiques and rewrites, up to 4 rounds. Large gains on style and preference tasks, almost none on math.
numbers: GPT-4: Dialogue preference 25.4 to 74.6; Code Optimization 27.3 to 36.0; Math Reasoning 92.9 to 93.1 (+0.2). ChatGPT Math 74.8 to 75.0; GPT-3.5 Math 64.1 to 64.1. Abstract claims about 20% absolute average gain.
limits: Preference tasks are scored by humans and by GPT-4 (82, 68, 71% agreement with humans on three tasks); same-family judge. Base prompts were not tuned (Kamoi unfair-settings point).
agent_relevance: Self-refine works where quality is a matter of degree; it does not fix hard logic. Use only where code has a check.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine: why math does not improve
finding: The authors trace the weak math result to failure to find the error: the critique says everything is fine. With an oracle that says when the answer is wrong, math gains appear.
numbers: ChatGPT feedback is 'everything looks good' on 94% of math instances. Oracle feedback (Appendix H.1): GPT-3 +4.8, GPT-4 +0.7 points on math.
quote: ChatGPT feedback for 94% instances is 'everything looks good'
limits: Oracle gain is small for GPT-4 because it was already near 93%.
agent_relevance: Evidence that detection, not rewriting, is the bottleneck. Aligns with S4 (test) feeding S5 (revise).

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine: feedback quality ablation
finding: Specific, actionable feedback beats generic feedback, which beats none.
numbers: Code Optimization 27.5 vs 26.0 vs 24.8; Sentiment Reversal 43.2 vs 31.2 vs 0; Acronym 56.4 vs 54.0 vs 48.0 (ChatGPT, ChatGPT, GPT-3.5).
limits: Generic feedback is still the same model's text; no external ground truth.
agent_relevance: When revising, the slot should receive a concrete located failure, not 'improve this'.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: After a failed trial, the agent writes a short reflection into memory and retries. Gains rely on an external pass/fail signal (environment, unit tests, exact match).
numbers: ALFWorld: ReAct+Reflexion solves 130 of 134 tasks over up to 12 trials (+22 absolute over baseline). HotPotQA +20. HumanEval Python pass@1 91.0 vs GPT-4 80.1. Rust 68.0 vs 60.0. MBPP Python 77.1 vs 80.1 (lower than GPT-4). Leetcode Hard 15.0 vs 7.5.
limits: Uses environment, ground-truth answers or self-written tests as the signal; Huang and Kamoi flag this as oracle use. Self-written tests give false results: HumanEval TP 0.99, FN 0.40, FP 0.01, TN 0.60; MBPP Python FP 0.16, FN 0.59.
agent_relevance: The mechanism (write why it failed, retry with it in context) is cheap. Its value comes from the check, which fits G2/G3.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: baselines cannot learn from retries
finding: On HotPotQA, plain retry baselines never solved any task they had failed in trial 1 (temperature 0.7). Reflexion did.
numbers: ReAct-only, CoT-only and CoT(GT)-only fail to solve any trial-1 failures later; Reflexion retried until 3 consecutive failures; memory 1 to 3 reflections; 100 HotPotQA questions.
limits: Small test. Grading by exact match against the answer.
agent_relevance: A retry with a reason in memory differs from a blind resample, but only given a reliable fail signal.

source: Kim, Baldi, McAleer (2023) Language Models Can Solve Computer Tasks (RCI)
finding: Recursive Criticize and Improve helps on MiniWoB++ and on reasoning, but the reasoning runs stopped on ground-truth answers.
numbers: GSM8K zero-shot 77.95 to 85.43 with RCI (row order read from garbled table). Max 2 RCI loops, stopped when output matches ground truth. Without that feedback RCI has false-negative critics and underperforms in half the benchmarks.
quote: the RCI process is prone to false negative critics, subsequently leading to a decrease in performance
limits: Kamoi flags oracle stop and no penalty for breaking correct answers. Table 1 columns misaligned in extraction.
agent_relevance: Same lesson: a stop signal from truth, not from the model, carried the result.

source: Tyen et al. (2024) LLMs cannot find reasoning errors, but can correct them given the error location
finding: Splits self-correction into finding and fixing. Finding the first wrong step is poor for all tested models. Fixing is good once the step is given. Releases BIG-Bench Mistake (2186 CoT traces).
numbers: Mistake-finding: GPT-4 overall 52.87 with direct step-level prompting. Tracking shuffled objects GPT-4 62.29/65.33/90.67 across three prompting methods; GPT-3.5-Turbo 10.10/1.67/19.00. Backtracking with oracle location: correct traces lose 0 to 11 points, incorrect traces gain +18 to +44 (multistep arithmetic +43.92, Dyck +36.86). Random location: gains only +5 to +21 and losses -6.7 to -15.9.
quote: state-of-the-art LLMs currently cannot find mistakes reliably
limits: Only 45 correct traces per task, so data skew; net overall change depends on base accuracy (50% base gives 68.6%, 99% base gives 92.8%).
agent_relevance: Strongest direct support for G2: locate the failure with code, then ask the model to fix. A wrong location still costs.

source: Tyen et al. (2024) trained mistake classifier
finding: A small classifier trained on out-of-domain data finds mistakes better than prompting a large model, and can feed the backtracking step.
numbers: Claim from the abstract; the Section 5 classifier tables were not read.
limits: Exact classifier accuracy not recorded here. Treat as abstract-level only.
agent_relevance: A learned or code-based checker can replace the model as a locator.

source: Stechly, Marquez, Kambhampati (2023) GPT-4 Doesn't Know It's Wrong
finding: Graph colouring with GPT-4: self-critique makes it worse; a sound verifier helps, but the content of the feedback hardly matters.
numbers: 100 instances: no backprompt 16%; LLM self-verification: 1 of 100 correct; sound-verifier backprompts about 40%, but plain top-n sampling (n=15, t=1.0) also gives 40%. In 40 runs GPT-4 produced an optimal colouring at some point and its verifier never accepted it (39 hallucinated a conflict). Of 500 colourings (118 correct) it called 30 correct and was right 5 times; of 100 optimal ones it accepted 2. When told an edge is wrong it changes it about 94% of the time, even for random 'evil' feedback.
quote: blindfolded guessing does just as well as careful, crafted feedback
limits: One NP-complete task and one model.
agent_relevance: Verifier errors, not the revision step, are the failure. Sampling again matches elaborate feedback, so G7 needs a more-samples baseline.

source: Valmeekam, Marquez, Kambhampati (2023) Can LLMs Really Improve by Self-critiquing Their Own Plans?
finding: Blocksworld planning with GPT-4 as writer and verifier. The LLM verifier accepts many invalid plans.
numbers: 100 instances. Generator alone 40%; LLM+LLM backprompt 55% (3.48 iterations); LLM+VAL sound checker 88% (4.18). LLM verifier accuracy 61%: true positive 54/55, false positive 38/45 (84.45%). Feedback level matters little: binary only 37/50 (74%), plus first error 43/50 (86%), all errors 43/50 (86%).
limits: The abstract says self-critique diminishes performance but Table 1 shows 55 vs 40; the text credits extra attempts. Table 3 used 50 instances.
agent_relevance: A model judge calls an invalid plan valid about 84% of the time. Never let it be the stopper (G5, G10). Binary pass/fail from a real checker is nearly as good as rich feedback.

source: Gou et al. (2024) CRITIC: LLMs Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
finding: Tools (search, interpreter) give the feedback. Without the tool, the model's own critique adds nothing and sometimes hurts.
numbers: Free-form QA: CRITIC adds about 7.7 F1 on ChatGPT; CRITIC without tool adds -0.03 and +2.33 F1 on the two LLMs. Text-davinci-003 GSM8K: PoT 70.1; CRITIC 72.2 (+2.1); CRITIC without tool 68.3 (-1.8). Toxicity reduction 79.2%.
quote: the model's own critiques contribute marginally to the improvement
limits: Oracle variant corrects only wrong answers and is not realistic.
agent_relevance: Same pattern as Reflexion and Huang: the tool is the active ingredient.

source: Welleck et al. (2023) Generating Sequences by Learning to Self-Correct
finding: Train a separate small corrector on pairs of bad and better outputs with scalar or text feedback. A much smaller corrector than the generator still helps.
numbers: GSM program synthesis with GPT-Neo 1.3B: generator 8.57% to 21% (24% when only correcting wrong outputs). Multiarith 98 to 99% after correction, a 38 point gain.
limits: Needs training and a feedback function; small models, old benchmarks.
agent_relevance: Early founding result for learned correctors (Pair-SFT in SCoRe). Not scaffold-only.

source: Saunders et al. (2022) Self-critiquing models for assisting human evaluators
finding: Models trained to write critiques help humans find flaws. Gap analysis: models know more than they say as critiques, and the gap does not close with scale.
numbers: Assisted humans find about 50% more flaws; also 50% more of the planted flaws in deliberately misleading answers. Larger models self-critique better though their outputs are harder to critique. Rejection sampling on answers is a roughly compute-matched baseline for critique-based refinement.
limits: Fine-tuned critique models, human labelers, topic summarisation; not prompt-only. Founded the idea that recognising errors is easier than avoiding them, which Kamoi says holds only for easy-to-verify tasks.
agent_relevance: Verifying-is-easier-than-generating is the logic behind self-correction; test it per task type.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Teaching LLMs to Self-Debug
finding: Few-shot prompting to run the code, explain it line by line, and fix it. Works best with execution results or unit tests.
numbers: Spider text-to-SQL (no unit tests): +2 to 3 points, +9 on hardest level. TransCoder and MBPP with unit tests: up to +12. Matches or beats baselines using more than 10x candidate programs.
limits: Gains tied to real execution output; explanation alone helped less.
agent_relevance: Clean model of S4 test to S5 revise with execution output. Sample-efficiency claim needs matched-sample baselines (G7).

source: Olausson et al. (2024) Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation?
finding: When repair cost is counted in tokens, self-repair gives modest, uneven gains and sometimes none against drawing more fresh samples. Feedback quality is the bottleneck.
numbers: GPT-4 on APPS: 10 initial samples + 1 repair each is 1.05x pass@20; 2 initial + 10 repairs each is 0.97x pass@22. Human programmer explanations instead of GPT-4's own raise repaired-pass rate from 33.3% to 52.6% (1.58x). Stronger-model feedback beats both baselines at all budgets.
limits: HumanEval and APPS; Code Llama, GPT-3.5, GPT-4. Human study is small.
agent_relevance: Compute-matched test is the right yardstick (G7). Spend on diverse first attempts before heavy repair (G12).

source: Dhuliawala et al. (2024) Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination
finding: The model drafts, writes verification questions and answers them without seeing the draft, then revises. Works because checking facts one at a time is easier than writing the list.
numbers: MultiSpanQA F1 0.39 to 0.48 (+23%). Longform FACTSCORE 55.9 to 71.4 (+28%). Wikidata list questions: 17% of baseline answer entities correct, but 70% when each is verified by its own question.
limits: Kamoi names this the case where verification is clearly easier than generation (decomposable outputs). Factual tasks.
agent_relevance: Supports the task-type boundary: self-check works when the answer splits into independently checkable parts. Independent re-asking fits G4.

source: Kumar et al. (2024) Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning (SCoRe)
finding: Multi-turn RL on the model's own samples makes intrinsic self-correction positive. Plain SFT and STaR collapse to not editing or break correct answers.
numbers: Gemini 1.5 Flash MATH500: base 52.6 then 41.4 (-11.2); Self-Refine 52.8 to 51.8 (-1.0); STaR 53.6 to 54.0 (+0.4); Pair-SFT 52.4 to 54.2 (+1.8); SCoRe 60.0 to 64.4 (+4.4). Correct-to-incorrect 15.8% down to 1.4%; incorrect fixed 9.5% base to 14.5%. HumanEval (Gemini 1.0 Pro): SCoRe delta +12.2, base +3.0, Self-Refine -1.2, Pair-SFT -1.8. MBPP-R 47.3 to 60.6.
quote: the intrinsic self-correction gain of 4.4% is the first significantly positive delta
limits: Needs RL training with reward on both attempts; not prompt-only.
agent_relevance: The base model's second look breaks 15.8% of right answers. A frozen-model scaffold must gate edits by code.

source: Qu et al. (2024) Recursive Introspection (RISE)
finding: Fine-tuning for multi-turn self-improvement lets 7B models improve over five turns without an oracle. GPT-3.5 gains little on its own.
numbers: GSM8K 5-turn: Llama2-7B +17.7 points, Mistral-7B +23.9; GPT-3.5 only +4.6. MATH: Llama2-7B +4.6, Mistral-7B +11.1. Headline: Llama3-8B +8.2, Mistral-7B +6.6.
limits: Trained model; some baselines (Eurus-7B-SFT) lose points over turns (-10.1 on GSM8K in one column).
agent_relevance: Self-correction is a trainable skill, not a free property of prompting. We do no training, so we rely on code gates.

source: Kamoi et al. (2024) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey
finding: Survey to May 2024. No prior work shows successful self-correction from prompted-LLM feedback in general tasks under fair settings. It works with reliable external feedback and with large-scale fine-tuning.
numbers: Three research questions: RQ1 intrinsic on best-possible initial answers, RQ2 with external information, RQ3 better than other methods. Bottleneck is feedback generation. Unfair settings: oracle labels (RCI, Reflexion), weak initial prompts, unequal compute against self-consistency.
quote: no prior work demonstrates successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs, except for studies in tasks that are exceptionally suited
limits: Literature review, no reruns. Cutoff May 2024. Names easy-verification tasks (CoVe) as exceptions.
agent_relevance: The test for our scaffold: beat sampling more at equal tokens, starting from best-possible first answers.

source: Kamoi et al. (2024) Evaluating LLMs at Detecting Errors in LLM Responses (ReaLMistake)
finding: Benchmark of real, expert-labelled errors from GPT-4 and Llama 2 70B. Strong LLM detectors have low recall and are sensitive to prompt wording. Self-consistency and majority vote do not help detection.
numbers: 12 LLMs evaluated. Per-model recall table not transcribed.
limits: Exact recall numbers not recorded; use the paper.
agent_relevance: Error detection by a model is the weak link; do not let it be the only locator.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Understanding the Dark Side of LLMs' Intrinsic Self-Correction
finding: Intrinsic self-correction makes models waver between answers, adds prompt bias on simple facts, and causes human-like overthinking bias on complex tasks.
numbers: Models: ChatGPT, Llama (2-7B, 3-8B, 3.1-8B), DeepSeek, o1 family. Offers question repeating and SFT on correction data as fixes. Detailed tables not extracted.
limits: Numbers not recorded.
agent_relevance: Another view of why a second look flips right answers; supports repeat-the-question style fixes.

source: Tsui (2026) Self-Correction Bench: Uncovering and Addressing the Self-Correction Blind Spot
finding: The same injected error is fixed when presented as the user's but not when presented as the model's own. A 64.5% blind spot on 14 non-reasoning models.
numbers: Appending 'Wait' cuts the blind spot by 89.3%. Fine-tuning on 5,306 correction traces cuts it by 76.0%. Macro accuracy base / with Wait / reasoning model: Qwen3-32B 0.045 / 0.793 / 0.894; DeepSeek-V3 0.567 / 0.902 / 0.908. Reasoning models show a small or negative blind spot.
limits: Controlled injected errors, not natural ones; natural errors are caught in part when shown externally.
agent_relevance: Role framing matters: asking the model to check 'someone else's' answer may work better (test first). A Wait nudge conflicts with G1 unless a signal triggers it.

source: Pan et al. (2023) Automatically Correcting Large Language Models: Surveying the Landscape
finding: Early survey sorting correction by when (training, generation, post-hoc) and what feedback (self, external model, tools, human). Written before the 2024 critiques.
numbers: Downloaded and title read only; no numbers extracted.
limits: Not read in depth. Use Kamoi for verdicts.
agent_relevance: Map of methods only.
